subtitle: How a copper charter bound sea merchants, scripts and a port into one order

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle close-up of a gleaming copper plate held between two different hands against a backdrop of ships and palm-lined harbour
panels.action: Anandhan of the Manigramam and Yosef of the Anjuvannam stand side by side on Kollam’s wharf, their contrasting hands gripping a long copper plate as ships ride the Arabian Sea behind them.

dialogue.text: In 849, at Kollam, a single copper plate carried many scripts, many guilds and many gods into one binding promise.

i18n.hi: सन् ८४९ में, कोल्लम में, एक ही ताम्रपट पर कई लिपियाँ, कई संघ और कई देवता एक वचन में बँध गए।

panels.shot: wide aerial sweep over the Kerala coast, evening light catching backwaters and sea, camera gliding inland then out to harbour
panels.action: The Kerala coastline stretches like a green ribbon between backwaters and the Arabian Sea, with the small port of Kollam glowing in the slanting light as fishing boats and large stitched ships dot the waters.

dialogue.text: Long before modern maps, the Kerala coast was already a line of memory on foreign tongues, its pepper and rice tying distant deserts and cities to these backwaters.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक नक़्शों से बहुत पहले, केरल का तट परदेसियों की ज़ुबान पर याद की एक रेखा था; इसकी काली मिर्च और चावल ने दूर के रेगिस्तानों और नगरों को इन बैकवॉटर से बाँध रखा था।

panels.shot: medium wide harbour-level view, camera at waterline showing big foreign vessels beside local boats, bustling quay
panels.action: On the Kollam quay, large sewn-plank ships with tall masts lie moored beside smaller canoes; dark-robed West Asian traders, dhoti-clad locals and sari-wrapped women weave through bales and jars.

dialogue.text: By the mid-ninth century, Kollam had become a hinge between worlds, where Chera-Perumal power met Arab, Persian and West Asian sea routes.

i18n.hi: नवीं सदी के बीच तक, कोल्लम दुनिया के बीच का कुंडा बन चुका था, जहाँ चेर-पेरुमाल शक्ति अरब, फ़ारसी और पश्चिम एशियाई सागरी मार्गों से मिलती थी।

panels.shot: tight two-shot at shoulder level, slightly angled, focusing on faces as they watch the harbour
panels.action: Anandhan, in simple but fine South Indian trader’s dress with a palm-leaf ledger at his waist, and Yosef, in a long robe and head cloth, stand together on a pier, eyes following the loading of a ship.

dialogue.text: Among the guild banners and house flags were traders whose names the plates would preserve: the Manigramam and the Anjuvannam.

i18n.hi: संघों के झंडों और घरों के निशानों के बीच वे व्यापारी थे जिनके नाम इन पटों ने बचा रखे: मणिग्रामम और अंजुवन्नम।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Anandhan as he oversees porters, ledger in hand, with temple roofs visible in background
panels.action: Anandhan gestures calmly to a line of porters carrying sacks towards a warehouse, his other hand resting on a palm-leaf bundle; behind him rise tiled roofs and a temple gopuram in the distance.

dialogue.text: Manigramam, as later inscriptions tell, was a powerful inland and coastal guild, tying temple towns, markets and ports into one chain of credit and caravan.

i18n.hi: जैसा बाद के अभिलेख बताते हैं, मणिग्रामम एक ताक़तवर स्थल और तटीय संघ था, जो मंदिर-नगरों, बाज़ारों और बंदरगाहों को एक ही उधार और कारवाँ की कड़ी में जोड़ता था।

panels.shot: medium close on Yosef at a table under a palm-thatched shade, unrolling a foreign-looking document, sea behind
panels.action: Yosef sits beneath a palm-thatch shelter, unrolling a parchment covered in unfamiliar letters while a sailor from a West Asian ship leans over and points, the sea wind lifting the edges.

dialogue.text: Anjuvannam appears in many ports, its members marked in the record as a separate corporate body, linked by West Asian names, tongues and sea-god oaths.

i18n.hi: अंजुवन्नम कई बंदरगाहों में दिखता है; अभिलेखों में उसके लोग अलग निगमित दल के रूप में दर्ज हैं, पश्चिम एशियाई नामों, भाषाओं और समुद्र-देवता की क़स्मों से जुड़े हुए।

panels.shot: wide ceremonial hall interior, slightly elevated angle, with ruler and court assembled; copper plates on low table
panels.action: Inside a timber-pillared hall, the Chera-Perumal ruler sits on a raised seat, courtiers arrayed around; in front, on a low table, lie stacked copper plates beside styluses and lamps.

dialogue.text: In 849, a new request reached this world: Mar Sapir Iso, a Christian leader from the West Asian trading network, sought land and privileges for his community at Kollam.

i18n.hi: सन् ८४९ में, इस दुनिया तक एक नई अर्जी पहुँची: मार सपीर ईसो, पश्चिम एशियाई व्यापारी जाल से आए एक ईसाई नेता, ने कोल्लम में अपनी जमात के लिए ज़मीन और हक़ माँगे।

panels.shot: close-up on Mar Sapir Iso’s figure before the throne, seen from behind him, ruler in background
panels.action: A bearded figure in long robes, Mar Sapir Iso, stands respectfully before the ruler’s dais, hands joined, while scribes sit cross-legged nearby, ready with palm leaves and copper.

dialogue.speaker: Mar Sapir Iso
dialogue.text: Grant us ground, and we bind ourselves to this port and its king.

i18n.hi: हमें ज़मीन दो, हम अपने को इस बंदरगाह और इसके राजा से बाँध देंगे।

panels.shot: medium shot of scribes incising a copper plate, with a pile of earlier plates nearby
panels.action: Two scribes bend over a long, shining plate of copper, one holding it firm while the other carefully cuts curling letters into it with a stylus as a lamp flickers beside them.

dialogue.text: The answer took the form Kerala knew best: a copper charter, inscribed in the ruler’s name, setting out land, taxes, honours and obligations in lines that could endure centuries.

i18n.hi: जवाब वही रूप लेकर आया जिसे केरल सबसे ख़ूब जानता था: तांबे का फ़रमान, शासक के नाम पर खुदा, जिसमें ज़मीन, कर, सम्मान और फ़र्ज़ ऐसी पंक्तियों में लिखे थे जो सदियों तक टिक सकें।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of the engraved copper surface, letters crisp and deep, hand still holding stylus
panels.action: The camera lingers on the copper surface itself, etched with tight lines of Grantha and allied scripts naming Kollam, the land grant and a Christian establishment at Tarisapalli.

dialogue.text: Later scholars reading these plates would see more than church history; they saw a port’s governance mapped in metal, linking temple land, royal revenue and mercantile corporations.

i18n.hi: बाद में जब विद्वान इन पटों को पढ़ेंगे, तो उन्हें केवल गिरजाघर की कहानी नहीं दिखेगी; वे धातु पर उकेरा बंदरगाह का शासन देखेंगे, जो मंदिर-भूमि, शाही राजस्व और व्यापारी निगमों को जोड़ता था।

panels.shot: medium wide shot of courtyard outside the hall, guild representatives gathered, each in distinct dress
panels.action: In the courtyard, Anandhan, Yosef and other guild leaders gather, each marked by their different clothes and ornaments, as a herald calls out names from within the hall.

dialogue.text: The plates did not speak only of clergy; they named the corporate bodies whose consent and presence gave weight to the grant—Manigramam, Anjuvannam and others around the port.

i18n.hi: पट सिर्फ़ पादरियों की नहीं बोलते; वे उन निगमों के नाम लिखते हैं जिनकी रज़ामंदी और मौजूदगी ने इस दान को वज़न दिया—मणिग्रामम, अंजुवन्नम और बंदरगाह के दूसरे दल।

panels.shot: close-up on Anandhan’s face as he listens, light catching his eyes, faint tension in his jaw
panels.action: Anandhan looks up towards the hall, his features steady but intent, as the distant sound of a scribe reciting ‘Manigramam’ reaches him.

dialogue.speaker: Anandhan
dialogue.text: Our name on copper binds us to this land and these seas.

i18n.hi: हमारा नाम तांबे पर हमें इस धरती और इन समंदरों से बाँध देता है।

panels.shot: close-up on Yosef’s hands as he adjusts a ring and smooths his robe, listening
panels.action: Yosef’s fingers nervously adjust a simple ring as he hears ‘Anjuvannam’ proclaimed, his gaze turning briefly towards a ship mast rising above the palm trees.

dialogue.text: The record does not list their faces, but in these guild names later historians hear the presence of Jewish, Christian, Muslim and other West Asian-linked traders woven into Kerala’s coast.

i18n.hi: अभिलेख चेहरों की सूची नहीं देता, पर इन संघ-नामों में बाद के इतिहासकार यहूदियों, ईसाइयों, मुसलमानों और दूसरे पश्चिम एशियाई-संबंधी व्यापारियों की मौजूदगी को केरल के तट में बुना सुनते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot of a row of witnesses seated, each stepping up to mark the plate, camera at plate level
panels.action: A line of men from different communities moves past the copper plate; one after another they bend to leave small incised marks or symbols beside the main script.

dialogue.text: Then came the witness marks, the quiet core of the charter—signs cut into the copper in West Asian scripts, testifying that these distant merchant communities stood as legal actors at Kollam.

i18n.hi: फिर आए गवाह-निशान, फ़रमान का शांत दिल—पश्चिम एशियाई लिपियों में तांबे पर कटे संकेत, जो गवाही देते हैं कि ये दूर के व्यापारी समुदाय कोल्लम में कानूनी पक्ष बनकर खड़े थे।

panels.shot: extreme close-up of the witness area of the plate, showing different-looking scripts clustered along the margin
panels.action: The camera lingers on the margin of the plate where, beside the main inscription, shorter lines in different scripts curve and angle in unfamiliar ways, clustered like a small forest of signs.

dialogue.text: Scholars see in these lines the presence of West Asian scripts—evidence that the port’s law could be witnessed in more than one tongue and letter-form.

i18n.hi: विद्वान इन पंक्तियों में पश्चिम एशियाई लिपियों की मौजूदगी देखते हैं—सबूत कि इस बंदरगाह का क़ानून एक से ज़्यादा ज़ुबान और अक्षर में गवाह किया जा सकता था।

panels.shot: medium shot of the ruler indicating boundaries on a palm-leaf map to senior officials, with a temple priest and Mar Sapir Iso watching
panels.action: The ruler gestures over a rough palm-leaf plan that shows fields, a church complex and a road; a temple priest and Mar Sapir Iso stand on either side, listening as officials take note.

dialogue.text: The grant spoke of fields, taxes remitted, duties exempted, rights over labour and ceremonies shared, binding the new Christian settlement into a land already tied to temples and royal dues.

i18n.hi: दान में खेतों, माफ़ किए गए करों, छूटे हुए महसूल, मज़दूरों के हक़ और बाँटी गई रस्मों का ज़िक्र था, जो नयी ईसाई बसाहट को उस भूभाग से बाँधता था जो पहले ही मंदिरों और शाही लगानों से बँधा था।

panels.shot: medium shot of labourers and service groups at work around the granted land, some bowing to officials, others carrying loads
panels.action: Around the newly marked land, toddy-tappers, ferrymen and other service groups toil; some bow as a local official walks past, while a Christian deacon points out the boundary stones to them.

dialogue.text: The same plates that preserve a story of accommodation also list hierarchies and service obligations, reminding us that this was a graded society, not an equal field.

i18n.hi: यही पट जहाँ मेल-मिलाप की कहानी बचाते हैं, वहीं दर्ज करती हैं दर्जे और सेवा-फ़र्ज़, याद दिलाते हुए कि यह परतों वाली समाज था, कोई बराबरी का मैदान नहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Kollam waterfront at dusk, guild banners fluttering, new church roof visible among palm trees
panels.action: As dusk falls, Kollam’s waterfront glows with lamps; a new church roof rises among palms, near a temple and warehouses, while guild banners of Manigramam and Anjuvannam ripple in the sea breeze.

dialogue.text: From that point, the charter tied church, guild and crown together; each shipment, each tax-free cart, moved under rules etched into that copper.

i18n.hi: उस घड़ी से, फ़रमान ने गिरजाघर, संघ और ताज को साथ बाँध दिया; हर खेप, हर कर-मुक्त बैलगाड़ी, उसी तांबे में खुदे नियमों के साये में चलती थी।

panels.shot: close-up profile two-shot of Anandhan and Yosef watching a ship depart, faint smile on one, thoughtful look on the other
panels.action: Anandhan and Yosef stand side by side at the water’s edge, watching a laden ship pull away into the darkening sea, the faint light from the town behind them catching their profiles.

dialogue.speaker: Yosef
dialogue.text: Ink fades. Copper remembers.

i18n.hi: स्याही मिटती है। तांबा याद रखता है।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide shot, same harbour view shifting subtly through centuries as ships and buildings change
panels.action: The viewpoint over Kollam slowly changes through time: wooden dhows give way to different hulls; roofs rise and fall; yet a careful hand in a later century lifts the old copper plates in a lamplit room.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, when historians unrolled these plates, they did not just see a church grant; they saw a port’s experiment in making many communities trust one shared record.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, जब इतिहासकारों ने ये पटें खोलीं, तो उन्हें सिर्फ़ एक गिरजाघर का दान नहीं दिखा; उन्हें दिखा कि बंदरगाह ने कैसे कई जमातों को एक ही भरोसेमंद रेकॉर्ड पर यक़ीन दिलाने की क़सम की।

title_i18n.en: Quilon's Copper Plate of Many Scripts

subtitle_i18n.en: How a copper charter bound sea merchants, scripts and a port into one order
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक तांबे के फ़रमान ने सागरी व्यापारियों, लिपियों और बंदरगाह को एक ही व्यवस्था में बाँधा
